generation_method: One genuine original white-marble image reused as palette/grid/style anchor; two new actualimagegen reference variations (cloudgrey and faintgoldthreads). No rotation/copy masquerading as newly generated image.

tool_args.prompt: Create one square, high-resolution seamlessly tiling albedo texture for the bright Hanbaiyu white marble courtyard of a Chinese palace in a premium miniature 3D adventure game. NOT a palace scene. True flat orthographic overhead material scan. A regular grid of four by four generous white-marble paving slabs, narrow subtle pale warm-grey joints; luminous ivory-white and pale pearl stone (#F2EDE2, #EEE9E1, #DDD9D0) with delicate low-contrast grey mineral clouds and sparse very fine pale champagne-gold veins (#D2BB83). The gold is faint natural mineral veining, not shiny foil and not ornate gilded frames; no yellow tint filling the whole surface. Calm clean broad slab areas, lightly honed smooth surface, a little fine stone pore detail and gently softened edges, restrained natural variation between slabs. All slab widths, joints, mineral veins and base color continue correctly across all four borders and all corners when tiled 2x2 or 4x4. No dark outside border, no giant central emblem, no dirt patches, no cracks dividing the whole map. Uniform flat neutral diffuse light, no baked shadows, no directional illumination or global gradient, no specular highlights or glossy reflected windows; engine will create afternoon golden sunlight. Entire canvas is one edge-to-edge seamless tile, not a contact sheet. No perspective, text, labels, objects, people, animals or watermark. Square 2048x2048 requested; highest available native resolution.
